subject: screech owl
title: This Owl Carries Live Snakes Home, and It Doesn't Eat Them

scenes.text: This owl brings live snakes home to its chicks. Not as food.
Screech owls usually kill what they catch. But one catch arrives alive and wriggling: the Texas blind snake.
It's worm-like, up to eight inches long. Some slip free and burrow into the bottom of the nest.
There they eat insect larvae, the kind that would otherwise feed on the chicks.
Texas biologists checked more than 70 nests. Chicks living with snakes grew faster and survived more often.
So the owl isn't stocking dinner. It's hiring a housekeeper.

description:
Eastern screech owls carry live snakes back to their nests, and the snakes move in.
The prey is the Texas blind snake, a burrowing snake up to about 8 inches (20 cm) long. Owls normally kill prey before delivering it, but blind snakes arrive alive; some are eaten, others burrow into the nest debris and feed on insect larvae that would otherwise parasitise the nestlings. Baylor University biologists Fred Gehlbach and Robert Baldridge studied more than 70 nest boxes near Waco, Texas, and found live snakes in 14. Owlets in those nests grew faster (by up to 50 percent, in one account) and were more likely to survive.
Pest control or pet? What would you call it? Comment below.
first_comment: Live snakes turned up in 14 of the 70-plus nests the biologists checked. Pest control or pet: what would you call it?
